answer: The network enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes reach a horizon of consensus while 1,000 fakes stall. A verifier challenges agents with a random path across memory, forming a shale of access latencies that reject shared-cache entities. Within this grove, any agent failing the memory-latency challenge faces permanent lockout, assuming unique bus serials. Honest participants pay 100 watts per gigabyte, while fakes accrue prohibitive overhead, failing the timing tests and forfeiting all operational assets to ensure integrity.
